title: Characters by index
intro: A String keeps its characters in order, like an array: `charAt(i)` reads the one at index `i`, counting from 0, and `length()` counts them all. Click the character each call reads.

rounds.right: The first character is `{name}.charAt(0)` and the last is `{name}.charAt({name}.length() - 1)`: the indexes run from 0 to {last}.

why.click: That's `{clicked}`. Indexes count from 0 at the first character, so `{expr}` is {index} steps along from the start.
why.last: That's `{clicked}`. `{name}.length()` is {length}, so the last index is {last}: one less, because the first is 0.

rounds.right: A space is a character like any other: it has an index and it counts in `length()`. One past the last index there is no character at all.

why.length: `length()` counts every character, and the space is one of them. It's the last index that is one less than the length.
why.click: That's `{clicked}`. Count from 0: `{expr}` is box {index}, and the space has an index like any other character.
why.last: `{name}.length()` is {length}, so index {length} is one past the last character, at index {last}.
why.space: There is no box at index {length}: the indexes stop at {last}. Java doesn't make up a character for a box that doesn't exist.

rounds.prompt: Empty or blank? Judge each call.
rounds.right: `isEmpty()` asks whether there are no characters at all; `isBlank()` asks whether every character is whitespace. A String of spaces is blank, but not empty.

why.isEmpty: `isEmpty()` is `true` only when `length()` is 0. `{a}` holds {length} characters: count the boxes.
why.isBlank: `isBlank()` is `true` when every character is whitespace, or there are none. Look at each box of `{a}`.
